title: Official vendor Source regeneration is not byte-idempotent
observation: Two consecutive successful official Source generator processes produced different canonical Source identities with identical file count and total bytes. This is FAIL, not idempotency PASS.
suspectedOwner: generate-official-db-vendor-source.ps1 iterates ordinary Hashtable Keys for logical-database and output-bucket ordering; mbwDB and referenceFixture share 40_business_modules_schema.sql, so cross-process key enumeration can reorder complete sections without changing byte count.
diagnosticReplay: The next unchanged process produced zero per-file changes, proving the current byte state can repeat but not making ordinary Hashtable enumeration a deterministic contract. The prior identity transition remains the fail-close trigger.
repair: Schema generation now iterates the already-sorted canonical logicalDatabases array and a separately sorted unique sourceSchemaFiles array; the bucket is ordered and no shared output ordering depends on fileByDb.Keys. A regression requires the explicit loops and forbids the old loop.
verification: PASS: exact regression 4/4; two post-fix external generator processes PASS; second process compares every file below cpf-tools/db/vendor and cpf-tools/db/generated/current and reports changedCount=0; Product Source identity remains 207ece107b87b19673c813558ec1eaa1f74de1ffae260d552b6efbb3c4086dad.
next: Reopen only if an official generation process changes bytes without a canonical input change.
falseGreenForbidden: Do not accept semantic equivalence, sort generated SQL after rendering, ignore Source identity changes, or suppress the replay.
